title: Malta or Cyprus in winter: which is warmer and better for a break?
author: Brogan
intro: Cyprus is a degree or two warmer in winter and has mountains and space, while Malta is closer, smaller and packed with history you can reach by bus. Neither is beach weather from December to February. Here's how they compare.
seo_title: Malta or Cyprus in winter? Cyprus is warmer, Malta closer
seo_description: Cyprus is about 1-2°C warmer in winter, Malta is an hour closer and easier without a car. Neither is beach weather in January. Full winter comparison.

sections.heading: The short answer
sections.text:
- **Warmer:** Cyprus, by 1 to 2°C
- **Shorter flight:** Malta, about 3¼ hrs
- **Easier without a car:** Malta
- **January high:** about 16 to 17°C

Both are mild, sunny winter escapes that feel familiar to British visitors: they drive on the left and use the same three-pin plugs as the UK. But they're not beach destinations in midwinter, so think of them as warm-ish walking and sightseeing breaks.

sections.heading: Malta and Cyprus side by side in winter
sections.text:
| | Malta | Cyprus (Paphos) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Flight from London | about 3¼ hours | about 4½ to 5 hours |
| Time difference | 1 hour ahead | 2 hours ahead |
| November high | about 21°C | about 23°C |
| December high | about 17°C | about 19°C |
| January and February high | about 16°C | about 17°C |
| March high | about 17°C | about 19°C |
| Getting around | Buses, ferries, taxis | Car hire, mostly |

The temperatures are average daytime highs from our [Malta](/destinations/malta) and [Paphos](/destinations/paphos) guides. Both islands get most of their rain in winter, so expect a few wet days alongside the sunny ones.

sections.heading: Why choose Malta
sections.text:
Malta is small and dense, which makes it ideal for a short winter break without a car. In three or four days you can see:

- **Valletta**, the walled capital, with St John's Co-Cathedral and its Caravaggio paintings, and views across the Grand Harbour.
- **Mdina**, the quiet walled city on a hill in the middle of the island.
- **The Three Cities** across the harbour, reached by a short ferry or a traditional boat.
- **Gozo**, Malta's greener sister island, a short ferry ride away. See our [Gozo guide](/destinations/gozo).

The bus network reaches almost everywhere, and taxis and ride-hailing apps fill the gaps. Our [Malta in 4 days](/blog/malta-in-4-days) post has a full plan.

Local knowledge: Malta's Carnival takes over Valletta in the days before Lent, usually in February, with floats and costumes. It's a lively time for a winter visit.

sections.heading: Why choose Cyprus
sections.text:
Cyprus is much bigger, and it rewards a week with a hire car. From Paphos, you can explore:

- **Paphos Archaeological Park**, with some of the finest Roman floor mosaics in the Mediterranean.
- **The Akamas peninsula** and **Avakas Gorge**, good for winter walks when it's too hot in summer.
- **Aphrodite's Rock**, the legendary birthplace of the goddess, on the coast road to Limassol.
- **The Troodos Mountains**, with painted churches, wine villages and, in a snowy winter, skiing on Mount Olympus.

The east of the island around [Ayia Napa](/destinations/ayia-napa) is quieter in winter, with many hotels closed, so most winter visitors stay in Paphos or [Limassol](/destinations/limassol).

Watch out: many beach bars, water sports and boat trips stop for the winter in both countries. Check what's open for your dates before you book a trip around them.

sections.heading: Is either warm enough for the beach?
sections.text:
Not reliably from December to February. Daytime highs of 16 to 19°C feel lovely in the sun, out of the wind, but the sea is cool and most people don't swim.

If beach weather matters, go in **November** or **March**, when Cyprus in particular can still be warm. For proper winter sun, you need to go further south: our post on [winter sun with no jet lag](/blog/winter-sun-with-no-jet-lag) compares the Canaries, Madeira and others.

sections.heading: Costs
sections.text:
- **Prices:** winter is low season for both, with cheaper hotels and flights outside Christmas and the February half term.
- **Transport:** Malta's compact size and buses keep costs down. In Cyprus, car hire is an extra cost, but usually cheap in winter.
- **Money:** both islands use the euro, and cards are widely accepted.
- **Flights:** both have flights all winter from many UK airports. Cyprus has two airports, Paphos and Larnaca, so check which is closer to where you're staying.

sections.heading: So, which one?
sections.text:
- **Choose Malta** for a short break of three or four nights, lots of history, and no need for a car.
- **Choose Cyprus** for a week, a little more warmth, a road trip and countryside walks.

If you're torn, read our guide on [how to choose between two holidays](/blog/how-to-choose-between-two-holidays), or browse the [where to go in January](/destinations/where-to-go-in-january) and [where to go in February](/destinations/where-to-go-in-february) pages. Or add both to somewhere.party and let the draw decide.

faqs.question: Is Malta or Cyprus warmer in winter?
faqs.answer: Cyprus, by about 1 to 2°C. In January, Paphos averages about 17°C by day and Malta about 16°C.

faqs.question: Can you swim in Malta or Cyprus in winter?
faqs.answer: Some hardy swimmers do, but the sea is cool from December to March and most people don't. November is the last reliably warm month for a swim.

faqs.question: Do you need a car in Malta?
faqs.answer: No. Malta is small, and buses, ferries and taxis reach almost everywhere. In Cyprus, a hire car makes a big difference.

faqs.question: How long is the flight to Malta and Cyprus?
faqs.answer: About 3 hours 15 minutes to Malta and about 4½ to 5 hours to Cyprus from London.
